{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested (combined line):
#   -t 05-00:00:00
#   -c 10
#   --mem-per-cpu=10240
#   -G 1
#   -J 3sl
#   --export=ALL

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  -c 10 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=120h \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=10240MB has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, placement may not account for memory needs,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm -J 3sl is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

# Slurm --export=ALL: environment is typically inherited by the shell here.
# (No explicit directive needed in this portable Flux script.)

module load anaconda
conda activate ilab
export PYTHONPATH="/adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/tensorflow-caney"

# Slurm used srun; within Flux we run directly inside the allocation.
python /adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/senegal-lcluc-tensorflow/projects/land_cover/scripts/predict.py \
	-c /adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/senegal-lcluc-tensorflow/projects/land_cover/configs/20220620/land_cover_256_trees_srv.yaml
'
"
}
